quotes.quote: The Human Pathogen Capabilities Test (HPCT) is a text-only benchmark developed by SecureBio and modelled after VCT that measures a model's ability to assist with work on a set of specific human pathogens (immune-evasive influenza viruses, immune-evasive coronaviruses, chimeric coronaviruses, poxviruses) that were identified by a panel of experts as being especially high-concern for misuse.

HPCT covers practical virology topics including virus isolation, genetic manipulation, tissue culture techniques, and experimental troubleshooting. It specifically targets methods that are highly relevant for successful lab work on these pathogens.
100 text-only questions with a holdout set privately held by SecureBio
13 PhD-level virologists answering question subsets specifically tailored to their pathogen of expertise scored an average of 31.5%
Models reach ~60% and outperform 100% of human experts when compared directly
Not publicly available, shared on request with organizations and researchers with a track record of work on AI safety.

HPCT questions are typically presented in a multiple-response format which significantly reduces the probability of guessing correctly compared to multiple-choice questions. However, every question also comes with 10 mutually exclusive multiple-choice options for alternative answer formats. The questions in HPCT are deliberately challenging, targeting tacit knowledge that is hard to find outside of practitioner circles.

Human performance on HPCT was measured by assigning 13 PhD-level virologists to answer subsets of ≥10 questions specifically tailored to their pathogen of expertise. The majority of questions were answered by three expert virologists who had not seen the questions before. Experts were given 15–30 minutes to answer questions with any resources found helpful except the use of AI models or talking to colleagues. These experts achieved an average accuracy of 30.8%.
We use the UK AI Security Institute's Inspect evaluation framework with zero-shot prompting. Each benchmark uses a built-in solver and scorer suited to its question format.
The multiple-response benchmarks VCT, HPCT, MBCT use the multiple_choice() solver with multiple_correct=True .
All use the choice() scorer with default settings.
Models are evaluated at a minimum of 10 times, sometimes more due to reruns.
Technically: error bars are 95% confidence intervals on the model's mean accuracy, computed using the bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap with 10,000 resamples.
We average over 10 runs per model, so our results may differ from scores based on just one or two runs.
Second, the exact evaluation setup (system prompt, scoring instructions, the full context the model sees) often differs between reports, which can change scores.
We are currently not making the full logs available and only show the aggregated results.
Performance of publicly available models on biosecurity-relevant benchmarks. All results generated by SecureBio.

Included benchmarks: VCT, HPCT, MBCT, WCB, ABC-Bench, ABLE, LB-CloningScenarios, LB-LitQA2, LB-ProtocolQA, GPQA-Bio, MMLU-Bio, PubMedQA, and WMDP-Bio. Models must have scores on at least 4 of these 13 benchmarks to receive a BCI score.

On the Human Pathogen Capabilities Test (HPCT), Astra performed within range of the previous model generation, GPT-5.6 Sol.
On all three benchmarks, the model far exceeded the performance of human experts.

All benchmark results were collected with the highest available reasoning effort ("max"). All knowledge and agentic benchmarks were run using the Inspect AI framework (UK AISI) with 10 epochs per sample.
Knowledge benchmarks assess model knowledge via question-and-answer tests.
All knowledge benchmark results presented below were collected without tool use or agent harnesses.

The Human Pathogen Capabilities Test (HPCT) is a text-only benchmark developed by SecureBio and modeled after VCT that measures a model's ability to assist with work on select human pathogens that were identified by a panel of experts as being especially high-concern for misuse (immune-evasive influenza viruses, immune-evasive coronaviruses, chimeric coronaviruses, poxviruses). HPCT covers practical virology topics including virus isolation, genetic manipulation, tissue culture techniques, and experimental troubleshooting. It specifically targets methods that are highly relevant for successful lab work on these pathogens.
The Astra Pre-Release Checkpoint (without system-level bio-classifiers) and its railfree counterpart attained scores of 65.9% ± 0.4% and 65.4% ± 0.2%, respectively, on HPCT.
A 9.9% ± 1.5% refusal rate was observed on the system-level bio-classifier-exempt Astra Pre-Release Checkpoint; no refusals were observed on the Astra Pre-Release Checkpoint (Railfree).

Per-question analysis of model performance across a larger panel of models showed the presence of questions that neither the Astra Pre-Release Checkpoints nor GPT-5.6 Sol (checkpoint) could reliably answer, but that were correctly answered by model(s) from other developers, suggesting that HPCT still has headroom for model improvements
Both scores represent a small decrease from the 66.5% ± 0.5% attained by GPT-5.6 Sol (checkpoint) (Figure 3.3.1, see Appendix A.2.3 for more model scores).

The Molecular Biology Capabilities Test (MBCT), Virology Capabilities Test (VCT), and Human Pathogens Capabilities Test (HPCT) are part of a suite of evaluations developed by SecureBio and the Center for AI Safety (Götting et al., 2025; SecureBio, 2025).
